law.text: A vehicle shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction upon any curve, or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade, where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.
law.title: Turning on curve or crest of grade prohibited in certain circumstances

cases.description: Actual three-point U-turn on a genuine crest. Both incoming-lane views identify the subject beyond 500 ft throughout the completed maneuver; original body-ray evidence retained. Grade0.008,35 s/700 frames.

comparisons.description: Added compliant crest branch under the declared geometric visibility convention: a genuine grade crest, actual three-point reversal, and positive subject-body visibility from both incoming lane positions beyond 500 ft throughout the maneuver. The two approach views are virtual cameras; there is one physical approaching vehicle. Original pixels and 4× nearest-neighbor magnifiers are retained. The shallower 0.008 grade differs from earlier fixtures, so this is an additional branch rather than a matched one-variable comparison. Human recognition is not established; the unresolved meaning of near is not exercised because the visibility precondition is false.

labeling_note: For these three crest cases, the crest context is established by the surveyed geometry and the completed audit; no numerical “near the crest” cutoff is applied. During the recorded reversal, a direction is geometrically visible at 500 ft (152.4 m along its incoming lane) when any of nine actual body samples has a clear ray. A blocked approach during the reversal supports the expected violation label under this convention. These are sampled evidence-backed scenario labels, not an independently executed legal formalization.
remaining_requirements_note: The three selected crest-placement cases are complete for the reviewed recording assignment, as established by the completion audit. Under the stated visibility convention all three are expected violations; this group has no compliant contrast. Broader curve-branch coverage and additional unselected definitions are separate from this completed assignment.
